answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x at daily settlement peak with heavy writes; the binding constraint is absorbing write load without dropping customer writes. memory_b3 is the closest prior: headroom kept queues flat through a surge. A release is a plausible confounder (started ~30m before the climb), so memory_b1 is worth verifying, but that case was an error spike rather than write latency and rollback during peak settlement is a larger blast radius than adding capacity. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) fail fast and would sacrifice writes, which violates the objective—flagged as downstream value risk if chosen. Failover and read-replica routing are weakly indicated (no regional signal; load is writes, not dashboard reads). Uncertainty remains that this is a bad build rather than saturation; capacity is the intervention least likely to lose writes if the cause is mixed.
